$comment: Shared fixture for the credential-name rule (issue #57). TWO implementations read
this file — tools/validate-widget.js (build time) and CredentialNames.cs (install
time) — and both are checked against it in CI, so the rule cannot drift into
'the validator refuses it but the host installs it anyway', which is the exact gap
Add a case here BEFORE changing either implementation. Every entry should be a
spelling someone could plausibly type, not a synthetic string: the innocent list is
the one that keeps the rule honest, and most of it was collected from real
false positives caught during review of PR #55.

notes.userKeyboardLayout: Squashes to 'userkeyboardlayout'. An unanchored compound rule matched 'userkey' and failed a keyboard-layout select in the field — that is why COMPOUND is anchored at the end.
notes.secretary: 'secret' with no trailing word boundary. Guards the boundary requirement.
notes.patch: 'pat' needs a boundary after it, or every patch/path/patient property trips.
notes.PATH: Squashed-pass casualty if word boundaries are dropped.
notes.monkey: Ends in 'key' but 'mon' is not a credential qualifier — COMPOUND needs both halves.
notes.webhookEnabled: A switch about a webhook, not the webhook. WEBHOOK_VALUE requires the name to END at webhook, or to be url-ish.
notes.signedUrlExpiry: Holds a duration. URL_VALUE requires the name to denote the value itself.
notes.feedUrl: Deliberately innocent: most url properties are public (iframe, youtube). It takes a secrecy qualifier — 'privateIcsUrl' is flagged, a bare feed URL is not. The spec tells authors to declare 'secret' themselves when their own feed URL is private, because no name-based rule can tell.
